$comment: Generated by npm run agent:index (tools/agent-index.mjs) from source: do not edit. Read @design-library/core/AGENTS.md first.
paths: A path that starts with @design-library/core/ is inside the installed package: node_modules/@design-library/core/ in your project, packages/core/ in the library repository. Library pages are the hosted library.
rules: Views and content hold no styles: no class names, style props, CSS or raw values outside a component or template part.
Never fork, copy, wrap-and-replace or restyle a core component; use props, slots, data attributes, tokens or a template part.
Components read semantic roles or their own component tokens; never primitives (p.*), spectrum.* or set.* for function.
Content is pure JSON validated by its template schema; the content check (npx design-library-check-content) must pass.

Change brand colours with brandCss/applyBrand from @design-library/core/colour (in your project) or colour.config.json and npm run tokens (in the library repository); never edit generated token files.
Custom parts live inside one template, named {template}.{Part}, styled under @layer templates.

components.name: AlignmentPicker
components.summary: Where a box's contents sit, chosen on a 3 by 3 grid of points, as in a design tool's auto layout. Each point is one choice; the chosen one carries the accent mark, the others a quiet dot. The grid is one enclosure; its points stay bare at rest. Not for choosing among named options (use SegmentedControl or Select) or for a text's alignment (a SegmentedControl of text-alignment icons).

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A person, organisation, team or bot as a picture, their initials or an icon, in one of 13 sizes. The picture falls back to initials on a colour the name picks from the category set (the same colour wherever that name appears), then to an icon for the kind. People are circles; organisations, teams and bots are rounded squares. Presence, a state (verified, approved, declined, warning) and a count come through Badge, sized with the avatar; an activity ring shows someone speaking or typing now. Many people: AvatarGroup; with their name beside it: Persona.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Several people or teams in one row: overlapping (stack) or side by side (spread), at most `max` faces, the rest behind a "+n" button that lists everyone hidden with their name and role. Built from Avatar and Persona.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: Information the system set and the reader can't change: a state or category in words, a count, a "new" dot, a status dot with words, or a person's presence; on its own or pinned to the corner of an icon, button or avatar. Not for a value someone picked or can remove (a Chip), an action (Button) or navigation (Link). Never takes focus. One component for what other systems call badge, lozenge, label, state label, counter, status light and indicator.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Triggers an action. One component for text, icon and text, and icon-only buttons, at seven sizes, with two ways to show an operation in progress (three: inside, ring, fill). Not for navigation (use Link; `href` only for a destination that is the main call to action), on/off settings (use Switch), a menu of actions (use MenuButton) or one exclusive choice (use SegmentedControl).

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.summary: Related buttons side by side as one named group, such as a form's actions or a view's tools. A fundamental by the owner's definition, being that common; a product can still define its own group as a compound. Not for one exclusive choice that applies at once (use SegmentedControl), for a toolbar of mixed controls (use Toolbar) or for on/off settings (use Switch).

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A month of days to choose one day or a range, that zooms out the way the Windows calendar does: press the title to see the year's months, again for the decade's years, again for the century's decades; choosing one zooms back in. Previous and next page by the view's period; Today comes back. Built for DatePicker and DateRangePicker, and usable on its own on a page. Not for a date someone knows by heart and types faster (a birth date: a TextField or three NumberFields), or for times.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: Selects an item, or agrees to something, as part of a choice applied by another action, at three sizes, with a description line, a mixed state for a parent of partly checked children and an invalid state with its fix. Not for a setting that applies at once (use Switch), or for one of several exclusive options (use a radio group). Several related boxes go in a CheckboxGroup, which names them with a legend.

components.name: CheckboxGroup
components.summary: Several related Checkboxes named together by a legend, with an optional hint and one error for the set. Not for one box (use Checkbox alone) or exclusive options (use a radio group). A "select all" parent is a mixed Checkbox at the top of the group whose state the consumer derives from the children.

components.name: Chip
components.summary: A value someone picked and can change or remove (an input chip), or a filter they turn on or off (a filter chip). Not for information the system set (Badge), an action (Button, even a compact one), navigation (Link), or a binary setting (Switch). Sets of chips go in a ChipGroup, which owns the label, the keys and the overflow.

components.name: ChipGroup
components.summary: A set of chips under one label: values someone picked (input chips) or filters they turn on (filter chips, one or several). Owns the label, description, message, empty state, the "+n" overflow and the keys.

components.name: Cluster
components.summary: Children in a row that wraps onto more lines when it runs out of room (or keeps to one line), with one gap from a space role: the layout owns the space, so a view never needs a styled wrapper or a margin. Not for children in a column (use Stack) or for a row of actions on something (use the component that owns them).

components.name: Code
components.summary: A short piece of code or a key name inside text: a token, a prop, a path, or a key such as Enter. Not for more than one line or for code someone will copy (use CodeBlock).

components.name: ColourPicker
components.summary: A colour chosen by eye or by number, as in a design tool's inspector: a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, a separate opacity slider over a checkerboard, the numbers in one of five models (HSL first), a pick-from-screen button where the browser has one, and swatches. Inline as a panel, or (`trigger`) as a swatch that opens it in a popover, the way fields use it. Not for choosing among a few named colours (a RadioGroup of swatches) or for a theme's brand colours (the colour config).

components.name: DateField
components.summary: A date typed in its parts, day, month and year, in the locale's order: three labelled boxes, or one field of parts that step with the arrow keys. Not for choosing a date near today from a calendar (DatePicker, which uses the segmented form for typing).

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: One date, typed in the locale's order or chosen from the Calendar in a popover under the box. Typing is checked when the person leaves the box or presses Enter: a date it can't read, or one outside the limits, keeps the text and says what to type. Not for a date someone knows by heart, such as a birth date (type it in three NumberFields), or a range (DateRangePicker).

components.name: DateRangePicker
components.summary: A first and a last day, typed in two boxes or chosen on a two-month Calendar in a popover: the first press sets the first day, the second the last, with the days between previewed as you point. A last day before the first is refused with a message, never silently swapped. Not for one date (DatePicker) or for a fixed period such as "this month" (a Select of periods).

components.name: Field
components.summary: The anatomy every input shares: a label above (or beside) the control, an optional or required marker, a hint, one message line (error, warning or success) and a soft character or word count, all wired to the control by id. Not a control itself: it wraps one (or, as a group, several).

components.name: Flag
components.summary: A country's flag, drawn from the subset of the MIT-licensed flag-icons set (the same picture on every system; emoji flags show as letters on Windows). Decorative: the country's name or code beside it carries the meaning.

components.name: Grid
components.summary: Equal columns for things compared side by side (options, variants), as many as fit at `size.column-min` each, a gutter apart; rows sit a group's space apart. Below two columns' width it becomes one column, so it never scrolls sideways from 320 px. With `ratio` it draws two uneven columns instead (a wide and a narrow one, or a heading beside its content) that stack when their container is narrow. Not for a page's regions (use LibraryLayout), a column of unrelated content (use Stack) or a wrapping row of small marks (use Cluster).

components.name: Heading
components.summary: A section title with a semantic level independent of its visual size. Not for emphasis inside a paragraph, or for labelling a control (use the control's label).

components.name: Icon
components.summary: Shows one semantic icon from the active set, drawn in the current text colour. The library's own outline set is the default; a theme can draw the same names from a curated MIT or Apache-2.0 library (`setIconSet`, owner Q36), and a name that library lacks falls back to its first style, then to the library's own. Not for decoration, and never the only label of a control without an accessible name.

components.name: IconOverrides
components.summary: A few brand icons for one part of the page (MP24, Q113): inside it, each name given draws the brand's glyph in every component that draws that name; nested ones merge, the inner winning; every other name falls back to the site's overrides, then the active set, then the library's own. Behaviour only: no element of its own.

components.name: Illustration
components.summary: Drawn art, inline: an SVG whose colours come from five role classes (`ink`, `muted`, `fill`, `surface`, `accent`) on tokens, so one file follows light, dark and more contrast; whose groups marked `data-size` show by the illustration's own width; and whose parts marked `data-motion` (`float`, `pulse`, `draw`, `fade`, `spin`) move on the motion tokens. For photos and art that can't follow tokens, use `Image`.

components.name: Image
components.summary: A picture in a frame of a fixed shape that holds its space while it loads, shows a soft fill while it waits, and says what it was when it can't load. With a caption or a credit it becomes a figure.

components.name: Link
components.summary: Navigates to a URL or route. Not for performing an action on this page (use Button).

components.name: List
components.summary: Items that belong together. Static: notes, numbered steps, plain items or short names in a row. Select: a list a person chooses one or several items from on the page, drawn with ListItem like every popup list. Action: items that run or open something on the page (drill-in rows show a chevron), with optional groups and dividers. Not for navigation (use Navigation), term and details pairs (use DescriptionList), a choice in a closed field (use Select) or actions that belong in a popup (a menu: MenuButton).

components.name: ListItem
components.summary: One item of a list a person chooses from: a menu's action, a menu's checkbox or radio, or a listbox's option. The one list item every popup list uses, so menus and selects look and behave alike: the same heights, padding, hover, focus, selected and unavailable states, leading slot (icon, avatar, picture, palette or selection mark) and trailing slot (meta, shortcut, submenu chevron or check). Not for navigation (use Navigation) or rows of data (use RowList). Added on the owner's direction (F10, 2026-11-07): "Dropdown list should be custom list using the same list item component." Made exhaustive in F15.8 (Q28, Q42).

components.name: MenuButton
components.summary: A button that opens a short menu of actions or starting points, such as presets. One trigger, one list, no nesting. Not for a value that stays chosen and shows in the control (use Select or SegmentedControl), for navigation (use Navigation or Link), or for one action (use Button). Added for the Colour page's brand presets (owner, F7d, 2026-11-07).

components.name: Morph
components.summary: One box whose content changes state in place (Q65 P3, strategy S2, "fake the content"): the box stays, the old content fades out quickly on top while the new one fades in under it, and the height eases between them. Nothing blinks out and back: a dialog's form becomes its result, a card's skeleton becomes its content, a thinking row becomes the answer. A quick change of mind reverses from where it is (the leaving content comes back). Not for a value that changes within one control (its own transition), something opening in place (Reveal), or something arriving from nowhere (presence).

components.name: NumberField
components.summary: A number to type, step, drag or calculate, from a form field to a dense inspector row. Arrows step it (Shift ×10, Alt ×0.1), Page Up and Page Down by ten steps, Home and End to the limits; the − and + buttons repeat while held; dragging the glyph, icon or visible label scrubs it with the pointer hidden and locked (Shift ×10, Alt ×0.1, Escape puts it back). Typing takes units ("24px", or another of `units` to switch), arithmetic ("12*2") and changes ("+4"). Shows "Mixed" for a selection whose values differ and "Auto" where the value can be worked out; offers common values (`presets`) in a list at the box's end. Not for numbers nobody adjusts (a postcode, a card number: TextField with `inputMode="numeric"`) or a value whose position in a range matters more than its digits (Slider).

components.name: Persona
components.summary: An avatar with the name beside or under it, and up to two more lines (role, status, location). The avatar is hidden from assistive technology because the name is written next to it; its presence, state and activity are read after the name instead. Used in list rows, people pickers, comments and profile cards; a person's own profile can offer an Edit photo menu.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: An anchored surface beside its button that can hold controls: contextual help with a link (the toggletip), a short form or a set of filters, a confirmation by its button. It opens on a press, never on hover, and doesn't block the page. Not for a hint without controls (use Tooltip), for a choice from a list (use Select or MenuButton), or for anything that must be answered before going on (use Dialog).

components.name: Progress
components.summary: The one operation indicator, in two forms: a compact turning arc, and a bar that fills to a known share or carries a travelling segment when the total isn't known. No separate Spinner. Not for content loading: views and sections of known shape load as a Skeleton.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.summary: Exactly one of a few visible options, chosen as part of a form saved by another action: vertical or inline, with option descriptions, unavailable options, a related question revealed under the chosen option, and a tile appearance. Not for a setting that applies at once (a Switch, or a SegmentedControl for 2-5 views), several choices (CheckboxGroup), or more than six options (Select).

components.name: Rating
components.summary: Chooses or shows a score out of a few stars (reviews, feedback). Hovering previews a value; pressing the chosen value again clears it; words per value say what each score means. Read-only shows any fraction, such as an average. Not for a precise number (use NumberField or Slider) or a yes/no question (use SegmentedControl or Switch).

components.name: Reveal
components.summary: Opens and closes content in place (Q65 P4, strategy S3): the box grows from nothing to the content's height (grid rows `0fr` ↔ `1fr`, one mechanism in every engine, MD7) while the content fades in; closing fades it out quickly and collapses. Only what follows moves, inside the layout budget (R3). Interrupted, it reverses from where it is. Not for something that appears from nowhere over the page (a popover, a toast: their own enter and exit), or for content replaced in the same box (Morph).

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A scroll region whose scrollbar is drawn over the content, never beside it: the content has the same width and alignment whether it overflows or not. Native scrolling stays (wheel, touch, keys, find in page, anchors); only the bar is replaced, by a thin thumb at the region's end edge that can be dragged, with the track paging on a click. Use it for every scroll region. Not for the document itself on small screens, which keeps the browser's own bar.

components.name: Select
components.summary: One choice from a list that's too long, or changes too often, to show as options side by side, at seven sizes, with an optional leading icon, a placeholder, grouped and unavailable options, a loading and an empty list, and the commit states when the choice is saved. Not for two states (use Switch) or for a handful of fixed options always worth seeing (use SegmentedControl). With `search` it is the combobox: typing narrows a long list (F15.44; no separate Combobox, as a one-time code is a TextField type). Picking people or free tags as a value is TagInput's job. Owner F10 (2026-11-07): the list is the library's own, built from the one ListItem that menus use, not the platform's.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A placeholder in the shape of content that is on its way, inside the content's own wrapper, so nothing moves when the content arrives. A soft light passes across it a few times (`count.shimmer-passes`), then it holds still. Not for an operation (use Progress) or a control's own pending state (the control shows it). The region it sits in sets `aria-busy` and says, once, what is loading.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: Picks a number, a range or several numbers on one track by dragging or with the keys, where trying values and seeing the result at once matters more than an exact figure (a font axis, a price band, a volume). Marks draw a scale (graduated); `step` or `restrictToMarks` quantise it. Not for a value that must be typed exactly (pair a NumberField or use one alone) or for an on/off choice (use Switch). Shares of a whole use AllocationSlider.

components.name: Stack
components.summary: Children in a column with one gap from a space role: the layout owns the space, so a view never needs a styled wrapper or a margin. Not for a titled part of a page (use Section) or for items that should wrap in a row.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: A binary setting that takes effect at once, at three sizes, with an optional description and the label before or after the track. Not for choices applied by a Save button (use Checkbox) or for actions (use Button).

components.name: Text
components.summary: Body and supporting text in one of the composite text styles. Not for headings (use Heading) or text inside a control (the control owns its label).

components.name: TextArea
components.summary: Several lines of text, sent by a separate action (a comment, a summary, a note), at a fixed number of lines or growing with the text, with a character count, read-only and invalid states. Not for one line that saves on its own (use TextField), or for text that must autosave while typing.

components.name: TextField
components.summary: One line of text saved on its own when the person leaves the field (blur-commit), at seven sizes, with an optional leading icon, fixed prefix or suffix text, a Clear button, a character count and a hidden-text (password) form. Not for values that must be valid or saved together with others (put those in a form with a Save button), or for long text that autosaves while typing.

components.name: TimeField
components.summary: A typed time in parts: hours, minutes (and seconds), plus AM or PM on a 12-hour clock, in the locale's order. Each part takes digits and moves on by itself, steps with the arrow keys and clears with Backspace. Not for a duration ("1 h 30 min": a NumberField with a unit) or for picking from available slots (a list of times).

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short hint beside a control, shown while it's hovered or has keyboard focus: the name of an icon-only control, a truncated label in full, or a few words of description. Never holds anything to click, and never the only place information lives on touch screens. Not for help with links (use a Popover) or for errors (use the field's message). Icon-only Buttons and MenuButtons, and unavailable Buttons, carry this hint themselves (`useHint`): wrap one only for a shortcut or a side, and the wrapper's hint replaces the built-in one.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: A stack of headed sections that open and close in place: frequently asked questions, a long form's optional parts, settings grouped by topic. Not for one short "Help with…" passage (use a disclosure), for switching between views of one thing (use Tabs) or for content everyone must read (show it).

components.name: Agenda
components.summary: A programme in time order: each slot's time, then the sessions that run then, side by side when they're parallel, each with its kind, title, people and place. For a conference or a course day, an itinerary or a broadcast schedule. Days or tracks go in Tabs around it. Not for picking a date (Calendar) or for rows of records to sort (DataTable).

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message that stays in the content until its cause goes: a section's error with Retry, a warning before a costly step, a success at the end of a journey, an outage banner, a note on a passage. One tinted surface, the tone's icon with its word, a title, the description, actions and an optional Close. Not for an outcome away from where the person is (use `notify()`), a field's error (Field's message), the list of a form's errors (ErrorSummary) or a question that must be answered (an alert Dialog).

components.name: AllocationSlider
components.summary: Shares a whole (a budget, a week, a weighting) between parts that always add up to the total: the filled bar is what is adjusted. Dragging the boundary between two parts trades share between those two only; typing a share takes from the next unlocked part and says which. Inner segments are square, only the bar's outer ends are rounded. Not for independent values on one scale (use Slider with several thumbs) or for showing shares without changing them (use StackedBar).

components.name: Board
components.summary: Work as cards in columns by stage (To do, In progress, Done): drag a card to another column or position, or move it with its Move menu. The columns scroll sideways inside the board when they don't fit. For a kanban board, a pipeline of deals or applications. Not for a table of records (DataTable) or a single ordered list (List with reordering).

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: The path from the top of a hierarchy to the current page, for apps deep enough that people need to know where they are and go back up (files, settings, documentation). Not for steps in a process (use a stepper) or for a flat app's sections (use Navigation or Tabs).

components.name: Canvas
components.summary: A design document drawn from data: frames with their names above them, and rectangles, ellipses and text inside, at a zoom, in a surface that scrolls both ways. Pressing a shape selects it; the selected one shows the accent outline, corner handles and its size. For an editor's working area or a preview of a layout drawn as boxes. Not for charts (StackedBar) or pictures (Image).

components.name: Card
components.summary: A bounded group of content about one thing: a picture, a title, one or two lines on what it's about, a line of facts and the card's own actions. The whole card can be one link. For a row of facts in a table use DataTable; for a number with its change use Statistic.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: A row of slides shown one (or a few) at a time: a scroll-snap track that a swipe, a trackpad, the arrow keys, the previous and next buttons or the picker moves. Optional peek, loop and autoplay with a visible Pause. Follows the WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern (tabbed picker). Not for content everyone must see: a carousel hides most of its slides.

components.name: ChatMessage
components.summary: One message in a conversation with an assistant: a person's message as a bubble at the end of the line, an assistant's reply as full-width rich content, with pictures and files sent with it and its actions. The content is composed by the caller (or mapped from data by a view), so a reply can hold any component. Not for messages between people (a comment thread) or for the whole conversation (ChatLayout places messages).

components.name: ChatThinking
components.summary: The assistant's thinking and tool activity before (and above) a reply: a quiet line with a turning arc and a shimmer while it works, which settles into a summary such as "Thought for 12 seconds"; opening it shows the reasoning or the steps. Not for the reply itself (ChatMessage) or for a long operation with a known total (Progress).

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Source code to read and copy: the code scrolls sideways in its own region, and a copy action at its top end confirms on itself ("Code copied") or says, under the code, when the browser won't allow it. Not for a token or a key inside a sentence (use Code).

components.name: ColourField
components.summary: One colour a person can choose, clear or leave undefined: a labelled swatch that opens the ColourPicker in a popover. Not for choosing among a fixed set of colours (use SegmentedControl or Select), or for showing a token's colour (use TokenSpecimen). Added for the Colour page's numbered brand colours (owner, F7d, 2026-11-07).

components.name: Composer
components.summary: Where a person writes to an assistant: one box holding what they've added (pictures and files), the text, and a toolbar with an add menu (files and tools), the chosen tool, dictation and Send, which turns into Stop while a reply arrives. The box grows with the text from one line, then scrolls. Not for a comment or a form's long answer (TextArea), or for chat between people.

components.name: ContextMatrix
components.summary: Values compared across contexts (light, dark, more contrast): each row's name once at the start edge, each context column rendered in its own context so a value sits on its true surface. Narrower than its columns, it scrolls sideways inside its own region with the names held; the page never does. Code in a cell stays whole. Not for a value that is the same in every context (say it once instead) or for facts with no context (use DataTable).

components.name: ConversationList
components.summary: The person's conversations with an assistant, grouped by when (Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days) or by project, the open one marked. Each row opens its conversation; its More menu (Rename in place, Share, Archive, Delete) shows on hover, on focus and on the open row, so a long list reads as titles. Not for the app's main navigation (Navigation) or a list of things to choose from (List).

components.name: DataTable
components.summary: Structured facts to compare in rows and columns, such as a component's props or its keys. The first column heads each row. Wider than the page, it scrolls sideways in its own region; the page never does. One enclosure, one hairline between rows, a header row set apart by tone. Not for a list of named values read one by one (a token reference), for term and details pairs (use DescriptionList) or for layout.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: Term and details pairs, such as what a component uses and what uses it: the terms share one column as wide as the longest term (at most `c.description-list.term-width` and three fifths of the list), the details take the rest. The columns come from the list's own content, never the page or the window, so it fits a page and a narrow inspector. Not for comparing several facts across rows (use DataTable) or for a list of equal items (use List).

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: Blocks the page until a question is answered or a short task is done: a title, a description, a body and the answers. Not for something people can ignore (use a notification), for a short confirmation by its button (use a popover) or for a side task while the page stays usable (use a side sheet). Most deletes need no dialog: do them with an undo in an auto-dismissing notification (owner rule).

components.name: EmptyState
components.summary: What a list, table, card or view shows when it has nothing: in the content's own wrapper at its least size, it says what would be here, why it's empty and what to do. The wrapper's toolbar, search and Add stay where they are. Not for loading (Skeleton) or a failure to load (Alert with Retry); not for a table cell (a dash with the name "None").

components.name: ErrorSummary
components.summary: The list of a form's errors at its top after a failed submit: "There is a problem", then one link per error that takes the person to its field. Built on Alert's error tone in the section placement. Not for one error near its field (Field's message does that) or for a failure of saving (an Alert with Retry).

components.name: Example
components.summary: A working specimen: a title and one line, the live preview in one outline, and its source behind "Show the code". Not for a screenshot or a static picture of a component, or for a demo with no source to show.

components.name: FileUpload
components.summary: Choosing files to send: a "Choose files" button, a drop area that also takes dragged files, and the list of files with each one's own progress, then done, or failed with Retry, and Remove. Not for picking a picture to crop (an image editor) or attaching files to a message (the composer's own button).

components.name: FloatingBar
components.summary: A small bar that floats over a whole screen at the window's bottom end corner and stays there while the page scrolls: for a few controls that belong to the frame around a screen rather than the screen itself, like a preview's light and dark switch. Not for a screen's own actions (Toolbar), messages (Notifications) or a page's footer.

components.name: Footer
components.summary: The foot of every page of a site: where else to go, the small print and who runs it. Quiet, on the sunken surface, the full width of the window with the page margin inside. Not for an app's status bar or a form's actions (use a Toolbar or the form's own buttons), or for a page's last section (use Section).

components.name: GradientEditor
components.summary: Edits a gradient's colour stops on a bar painted with the gradient itself: drag a stop to move it, click the bar to add one with the colour already there, drag a stop off the bar or press Delete to remove it (two always remain). The selected stop's colour opens the ColourPicker (Enter on a stop too); its position takes an exact number. Flip and Distribute evenly rearrange every stop. Not for one colour (use ColourField) or for shares of a whole (use AllocationSlider).

components.name: ImageGeneration
components.summary: The wait while an image is generated, in the finished picture's own frame: a moving field (the owner's watai stipple, the AI colours, a sharpening preview or a quiet shimmer) under one line saying what's happening, then the picture fading in where the wait was. A failure stays in the same frame with its reason and Retry. Not for loading an existing picture (Image with Skeleton) or for a view's skeleton.

components.name: ImageGrid
components.summary: A set of pictures arranged as one: equal frames, a quilt with features, masonry columns or justified rows. Each layout keeps every column at least `c.image-grid.min` wide and falls to fewer as the place narrows, so nothing scrolls sideways. With `onSelect`, a picture opens (into a Lightbox). For pictures one at a time use Carousel.

components.name: IndexList
components.summary: A way into each page of a set: its name as a link and one line on what it holds, in as many columns as fit. Not for an app's own navigation between its pages (use Navigation) or for a list of plain names (use List).

components.name: InlineEdit
components.summary: Text shown as text until it's pressed; then a field in the same place and size. Enter or leaving the field saves, Escape cancels; a failed save keeps the field open with what was typed and Retry. For titles, names and single values that change now and then, where a form would be heavier than the edit. Not for values that must be checked together (use a form) or for long text (use TextArea).

components.name: Lightbox
components.summary: The pictures of a set, one at a time and as large as the window allows, over the page: opened from an ImageGrid or a Card, with Previous and Next, a counter and the caption. Built on the same native modal dialog as Dialog.

components.name: MediaPlayer
components.summary: Plays a video or a piece of audio, with its caption: a file this product serves, with the browser's own controls and its captions, or a video on YouTube or Vimeo behind a privacy-friendly poster that loads the remote player only when play is pressed. Not for a picture (use Image), a set of pictures (use Carousel or ImageGrid) or a video that plays by itself as decoration (don't: motion that can't be paused fails WCAG 2.2.2).

components.name: Mentions
components.summary: A text area where typing "@" suggests people to mention: keep typing to narrow the list, choose one, and their name is written into the text after the "@". For comments, messages and notes that notify or credit someone. Not for picking people as a field's value (use a Combobox or TagInput).

components.name: MessageActions
components.summary: The actions under one chat message, as icon buttons with tooltips: Copy (confirms "Copied"), Edit, Good and Bad response, Read aloud, Share, Try again, Branch in a new chat, and the versions a message has. Only the actions given show, in that order, so a person's message gets Copy and Edit and a reply gets the rest. Not for actions on the whole conversation (the header's menu).

components.name: Navigation
components.summary: Moves between the pages of an app or a document set: headed groups of pages and families of pages, the current page marked. Groups are told apart by a heading and the largest space; a family's pages sit under its name, indented so their names line up with it, and open and close together. A family inside a family indents one more step (three at most). Not for actions (use Button), for choosing how content shows (use SegmentedControl) or for the steps of a task.

components.name: Notifications
components.summary: The one place for outcomes the person can't see where they are: background work finished or failed, a change that left the view with Undo, a partial success. Place it once at the app's root; anything calls `notify()`. Pills sit at the bottom, centred, newest nearest the edge, at most three, the rest counted as waiting. Not for a field's save (its own tick), a validation error (on the field), a failure of the view in front of the person (that scope's Alert) or a question (a Dialog).

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: The head of a page: where it sits, its title, what it's for and where it comes from. Not for the app's identity (use TitleBar) or for headings inside a page (use Section).

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Moves between the pages of a long set of results or the pages of a guide, after the content. Not for steps in a process (use a stepper) or for a few sections of one thing (use Tabs).

components.name: Pane
components.summary: A working side pane beside the page: a heading, a close action, its sections and one status line at its foot. The layout places it (LibraryLayout's aside); it is never a modal and never takes focus on its own. Not for a dialog that needs an answer before going on (a Dialog compound, later) or for page content (use Section).

components.name: PropertyRow
components.summary: One row of a design tool's inspector: compact fields in a two-column grid with an action column at the end, as Figma's properties panel lays out X | Y, W | H and rotation | radius. Rows stack inside a PropertySection. Use small (xs) fields with inline glyphs or icons and hidden labels; the section's heading names the group. Not for a form's fields (use a Stack of fields with visible labels) or for facts (DescriptionList).

components.name: PropertySection
components.summary: One group of an inspector or a settings panel: its heading and the actions on the whole group on one row, then its rows. Groups sit apart by the panel's gap; nothing draws a box or a rule between them. Not for a page's sections (use Section) or for a group a person opens and closes (use Accordion).

components.name: Quote
components.summary: Words someone said or wrote, set apart from the text around them, with who they're from and where: a testimonial, a recommendation, a line from an interview or a book. Put several in Cards for recommendations, or one per slide in a Carousel for voices. Not for repeating a line of the same article for emphasis (a pull quote is Heading or Text at a larger size) or for code (use CodeBlock).

components.name: RowList
components.summary: Rows of named facts, one hairline above each and no enclosure, in proportional columns that stack below the small breakpoint: a reference list read from top to bottom (token rows, scales, specimens beside their values). Not for comparing values across columns with a header row (use DataTable) or across contexts (use ContextMatrix).

components.name: SchemeControl
components.summary: Lets a person choose the colour scheme, applies it at once without a page flash and remembers it for the next visit. Three forms over one choice (ID3): a three-way choice of light, dark and system (the default, because following the system is a third answer, not "off"); a dark-mode Switch for a settings list, where off means light; and an icon button named by what it does, for a header with no room for either. Not for contrast or density (use SegmentedControl or Switch with your own setting). Composes SegmentedControl, Switch and Button and adds no styles of its own; the choice itself is `useScheme`, which a site can use to drive any control.

components.name: ScreenPreview
components.summary: A whole screen shown in a window of a chosen width, live, so its narrow behaviour is the real thing (media and container queries answer to the frame, not to the page around it). For documenting a layout or a preset. Not for embedding third-party content or for a component's own example (Example).

components.name: Section
components.summary: A titled part of a page: a heading, a short intro that holds for everything in it, then its content. Not for the page's own head (use PageHeader) or for grouping that space alone already shows.

components.name: SectionedForm
components.summary: A form in sections, as an inspector's or a settings page's: from `twoColumnFrom` of its own width, a list of the sections (titles, under their group headings) beside the chosen section's fields; narrower, every section in turn, one below the other. Each section is a PropertySection. Not for sections a person opens and closes (Accordion), for switching between unrelated panels (Tabs) or for a list beside a document (ListDetail).

components.name: Sheet
components.summary: A panel from the start, end or bottom edge, for a side task or the details of one item while its list stays in view: a title, the body and the answers. Not for a question that needs an answer first (use a Dialog), for a short choice by its button (use a Popover) or for a pane the layout keeps on screen (use Pane).

components.name: SiteHeader
components.summary: The top of a website: the name (and mark) linking home, the main places, and one or two actions. When its own width is narrow (below 48 rem) the places move behind a Menu button and open as a list under the bar. Not for an app's top bar (TitleBar) or for navigation within one section of pages (Navigation).

components.name: StackedBar
components.summary: Parts of a whole by status, in one bar: inner segments are square so small parts stay legible, a hairline of the surface between them; only the outer ends of the whole bar are rounded. A legend under the bar names every part with its share. Status colours only: categorical series arrive with the first chart, from the spectrum. Not for progress over time (use Progress) or for comparing values that aren't parts of one whole.

components.name: Statistic
components.summary: A number that matters, with what it counts, its unit, its change since the last period and an optional trend line: the figures at the top of a dashboard or a report. Put several in a Grid, or one in a Card for a tile. Not for a table of numbers (use DataTable) or a share of a whole (use StackedBar).

components.name: TableOfContents
components.summary: Links to the parts of the page: "on this page" beside or above long content, or a letter jump over an A to Z list. The part being read is marked as the page scrolls. Inside the core router an entry keeps the route and moves focus to its heading; without one it is a plain in-page link. Not for links between pages (use Navigation or SiteHeader) or for a numbered index of pages (use IndexList).

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Switches between panels of related content in place, or between the pages of one section as links. Not for a value that changes what one view shows (use SegmentedControl), for steps in a process (use a stepper) or for an app's main sections (use Navigation).

components.name: TagInput
components.summary: Turns typed text into removable tags: Enter or a comma ends a tag, a pasted list splits into tags, repeats and a maximum are refused and said, and a check can mark a tag invalid while keeping it. Not for choosing from a known list (use a Combobox when it lands) or for one value (TextField).

components.name: TitleBar
components.summary: The top of an app: who it is (name, version, status) at the start and app-wide controls at the end. Not for page titles (use PageHeader) or for navigation between pages (use Navigation).

components.name: TokenSpecimen
components.summary: Draws one design token so its value can be seen, the drawing chosen by what the token is: one component for every kind, not a variant per kind. The values come from the tokens themselves, so the specimen is always current. Not for content: a chart's bar is a StackedBar, a status message is text with a tone.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A row of related actions, or a control or status with its actions: one gap, the start part growing, the actions wrapping without overlap. The row draws no enclosure, so its buttons stay as they are. Not for an app's identity and global actions (use TitleBar) or for a choice between options (use SegmentedControl).

components.name: TreeView
components.summary: A hierarchy to browse and choose from: layers in a design file, folders and files, sections of a long document. Each row can open to show its children; one row is selected. Not for site navigation (Navigation) or a flat list of options (List, Select).

components.name: VisibilityToggle
components.summary: The eye (and padlock) toggle (Q125): the established, universal pattern for showing or hiding one thing in a list (a layer, a fill, a stroke, an effect, a page colour) and for locking it. A pressed icon button: its icon is the state (eye or eye with a slash; closed or open padlock), so it carries no fill when on. Unlike other toggle buttons it needs no written reason where it's used: it is the library's named pattern for these two meanings. For any other binary setting use Switch.

components.name: AppLayout
components.summary: A working app: a collapsible sidebar of places, a header, and the view, which scrolls on its own; optionally a details column beside it. For tools people work in all day: a tracker, an admin, a dashboard, a mail client. Not for a conversation (ChatLayout), an editor with a canvas (EditorLayout) or a website (SiteLayout).

components.name: ChatLayout
components.summary: A conversation with an assistant: a collapsible sidebar of chats, a header, the messages in a reading column that scrolls on its own, and the composer under it that never scrolls away. While the person is at the newest message, new words keep them there; once they scroll up, a Jump to newest button appears. A new chat centres a greeting and the composer instead. Not for a document beside a list (ListDetail) or a page of reading (PageLayout).

components.name: EditorLayout
components.summary: An editor: a bar across the top, a panel at each side that can be hidden, and the working area between them that takes the rest of the room. For a design tool, a diagram or map editor, a page builder. In a narrow window an open panel floats over the working area from its own edge. Not for a list beside a document (ListDetail) or a conversation (ChatLayout).

components.name: Frame
components.summary: Presents one piece of content so it stands on its own (owner Q88, docs/spacing.md#framing-presenting-one-piece-of-content): its own room sized to the window and isolated from what's around it. To spacing it's one unit (Q94): its parent places it at the parent's gap, measured from its outer edge, and inside it the spacing method starts again (its content is a tree of its own). Never a box: space first, an optional edge-to-edge tone second, no border or shadow. It steps down with the window (Q89): a peek stage becomes a feature on a narrow window and its content's height on a short one; a feature drops to flow when its space would pass a third of the window's height. Not for lists, grids, forms or anything a person works through (they flow), and at most one stage per page. Frame only what gains from being read alone (Q91): a task or reference page (tickets, a schedule, a list, a detail page) never frames its heading away from the content people came for.

components.name: Hero
components.summary: A view's opening: an eyebrow, the title set large, a lead, the one or two main actions and, if it helps, a picture. For a landing page or the opening of a long page's section. Not for the head of an ordinary or documentation page (use PageHeader) or for a section's heading (use Section).

components.name: LibraryLayout
components.summary: A screen with a header, a navigation region, a main region and an optional side pane, for catalogue-style apps. Not for single-task screens or dialogs; use a focused layout there.

components.name: ListDetail
components.summary: A list beside the chosen item's detail, both from the top: an inbox, settings, files, people. It measures the room it is given, not the window: where both don't fit, one shows at a time and the detail has a Back. It only lays out the caller's list and detail; their content, selection and empty states stay theirs. Not for a page's reading column (use PageLayout) or for a side task over the page (use Sheet).

components.name: PageGrid
components.summary: A page's composition grid (DesignUp, owner 2026-11-12 23:54, 2026-11-13 02:27): the page is rows; a row's cells divide its span of the page's twelve columns (`span`, at least 3 where a row has more than one cell, so at most four across); a cell holds more rows or is a slot for one block or fundamental. Spans are absolute at every depth, so a nested row only subdivides its parent's span and every cell lines up with the page's columns. An empty slot keeps its size (`data-empty`, setting `--c-page-grid-empty-size`), so a preview lays out as the editor does. The edits an editor makes (split in two, merge two empty cells, move a border, add a row) are `@design-library/core/page-grid`. Rows sit a chosen stack step apart (`gap`); columns a fixed gutter apart. A row whose narrowest cell would be under `size.column-min` stacks its cells in source order, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px. The only way to put blocks side by side on a page: blocks never nest a page inside themselves. Not for things compared side by side inside a block (use Grid), an app's regions (use AppLayout or EditorLayout) or free positioning (there is none).

components.name: PageLayout
components.summary: One page's content as a reading column: its header, then sections spaced as their own groups, up to a widest size. Not for the app's frame (use LibraryLayout) or for a dense working screen.

components.name: SiteLayout
components.summary: A website's page: the site header at the top (it stays while the page scrolls, on the chrome material: frosted when the setting is on, with its hairline only while content is under it), the page's parts in one centred column spaced as sections, and the footer across the full width. The window scrolls; the margins hold at every width. Not for an app with its own panes (ChatLayout, ListDetail) or for documentation with a side navigation (LibraryLayout). Frame settings (ID4): the column's width, margin, gap and the space above the first band are theme settings, set with `applySettings` from `@design-library/core/theme` (the allow-list is `tokens/settings.json`).

components.name: StickyBar
components.summary: A bar of controls that sticks within its section: the first child of a section (or any block), it sticks under the site header (`--dl-chrome-block`, which SiteLayout measures) once its own place scrolls away, only while its parent is on screen, and leaves with it. Stuck, it takes the floating material and a raised shadow (`data-stuck`); at rest it has no fill or shadow, and its geometry never changes between the two. Not for the page's own header (SiteLayout's header already sticks), for a toolbar that floats over a canvas (use FloatingBar) or for a bar that should stay for the whole page (put it in the header). Added for DesignUp's Talks finder (LR4, 2026-11-12): "Search and filters bar: this should be a sticky header within the section when it scrolls out of view."

components.name: conference.Countdown
components.summary: How long until a moment a person is waiting for (the doors opening, a ticket sale closing): the words, then the time left in days and hours, or hours and minutes on the last day, in the reader's language. Once the moment passes it says `passed` instead. A Conference template part (Q64): it lives only in this template's scope. Not for a timer a person starts and stops, or for a length of time that's already known (write it as text).

components.name: conference.SponsorWall
components.summary: The sponsors of an event by level, largest first: each level a heading, then its sponsors as tiles (their wordless mark when there is one, the name set in the display face, and a few words under it), larger tiles and marks for higher levels. A tile is one quiet surface with no border; a sponsor with a site has its name as the link. A Conference template part (Q64). Not for logos of customers on a company's home page (a logo strip), or for people (use Persona).

components.name: conference.SponsorsLayout
components.summary: A sponsors section: an intro column (why, the time left, how to join) beside the sponsors by level in a wide window, and above them in a narrow one. A section layout: it goes in a page layout's main region (SiteLayout's), never wraps one. A Conference template part (Q64). Not for a list of people (use a grid of Persona) or a sponsor's own page.

schemas.title: Template assets, version 1
schemas.description: A template's pictures by id. Content names a picture by its id; `src` is a file in the template's own folder; `alt` says what it shows.

schemas.title: Core block set, version 1
schemas.description: The standard block types every template may use (Q64). Each `$defs` entry named after a block type is that block's shape; `packages/core/render/blocks.tsx` maps each to core components. `settings.{Layout}` entries are the options of core layout components. Every word a person reads, including labels and messages, is in the block (Q64); words are plain text (backticks for inline code are the only mark); pictures are asset ids; `/layout` links point at a layout of the same template.

schemas.title: Collection, version 1
schemas.description: A typed list of like things a site shows in many places (DP12, DR21, DR22): talks, people, books, offices. Each item has an id unique in the collection; `item` is the JSON schema every item meets. Page documents and other collections point at an item with { "ref": "books/the-long-shore" } (the whole item) or { "ref": "books/the-long-shore", "field": "title" } (one value, a dotted path that follows references); a page whose route has `:id` and names the collection is each item's own page, and reads the item it shows with { "item": "title" }. schemas.title: Template content envelope, version 1
schemas.description: What every content file of every template shares (Q64). A layout's file has `layout` and either `regions` (documents: regions of blocks) or `record` (applications: one record the layout's schema defines), never both; an application layout that shows only the shared record has neither. A template's shared file has `shared: true` and the regions every layout shares. Pure data: no markup, styles or code.

schemas.title: Page document, version 1

schemas.title: Site document, version 1

schemas.title: Template manifest, version 1

frameworks.title: How the library works
rules: Look comes only from tokens; a view, page or content file never carries a class name, style prop, CSS file or raw value.
Components are sealed (no className or style props). Change them by the seam ladder: prop or variant, slot, context attribute, theme, custom part inside a template, then a reviewed core change.
Screens are data: a template manifest names layouts and regions; content JSON fills them; the renderer maps content to layouts, compounds and fundamentals.
Tiers depend downward only: tokens <- fundamentals <- compounds <- layouts <- templates. A fundamental never imports a compound.
Never edit a generated file (tokens.colour.json, tokens.space-shape.json, css/tokens.css, tokens/generated/*, agent/*, generated content schemas).
decide: Search packages/core/agent/index.json for an existing component, block type, layout or template before writing anything.
Pick the lowest tier that meets the need: a fundamental if it is universal, a compound if it arranges fundamentals for one need, a layout for named regions of a screen.
If nothing fits, take the first seam on the ladder that works; a custom part lives in your template as {template}.{Part}.

frameworks.title: The owner’s design rules
rules: Never a one-sided accent border (border-left stripe) on a card, button, callout or nav item; use a fill, tint, full outline, icon or badge.

A binary setting is a Switch by default; a Button with `pressed` (a toggle button) or a Checkbox only where a Switch doesn't fit the surface, with its reason written above it (`binary-setting:` comment, Q121, Q124); visibility (eye) and lock are established toggle buttons and need no reason (Q125).
Inner segments of a stacked or segmented bar are square; only the outer ends of the whole bar may round.

Pad once at the right interior level (one or two levels below the visual wrapper), never all around a wrapper or per leaf; scroll regions bleed to the surface edge with the scrollbar at the edge; never clip a focus ring.

Every scroll region is a ScrollArea: never `overflow: auto` or `scroll` on any other element, in CSS or inline, since that draws the browser's bar beside the content. Put ScrollArea where the region meets its surface's edge, with its padding on the content inside (its `inset`, or a padded child). A TextArea scrolls its own text and already uses the library's bar.
One component variant per need: no second pattern where one already does the job.
Notifications auto-dismiss; manual dismiss only when the person must read it.
decide: Before adding an accent, choose fill, tint, full outline, icon or badge, in that order of preference.
Before adding a variant, search agent/components/{Name}.json for an existing prop that covers the need.
Before adding padding, find the wrapper that owns the visual edge and pad the first content level inside it; keep the scroll container itself unpadded.

Before letting anything scroll, wrap it in ScrollArea (axis, maxSize, inset; contain only in a popup or modal) placed at its surface's edge; then run the scroll probe (tools/scroll-probe.js) on the screen.

frameworks.title: Presets
rules: A preset is a saved choice per category: colour, type, icons, space, shape, material. A global preset names one per category.
Built-in presets are read-only; user presets are saved beside them (design-library.presets) and sync across tabs.
Templates inherit the global preset; a template never hard-codes a category choice.
Choose at run time with @design-library/core/presets (applyGlobalPreset, applyCategoryPreset); change defaults at build time through the token config files.

Chrome is a context, not a size: a region that is app chrome (a sidebar of places, an inspector or property panel, a layers panel, a details column, an editor) carries data-density="compact" on its root, so text takes the small size and corners the shape's small radius. Content (a main view, a conversation, a page column, a canvas's document) stays in the default context. Never shrink chrome by passing size props to each control or overriding a radius. AppLayout's sidebar and details column and ChatLayout's sidebar are compact already; put it on an EditorLayout's root.
decide: The product owns this repository look: change the theme (config file, npm run tokens).
The app needs another built-in option: apply a category or global preset at run time.
A person wants to keep their choice: saveCategoryPreset or saveGlobalPreset.
A region looks too big or too round for a tool: ask whether it would change if the content changed. If not, it's chrome: set data-density="compact" on it, then run tools/context-probe.js.

frameworks.title: Colour
rules: Components read semantic roles only (color.text, color.bg-raised, color.border-control, state.*); never p.* primitives.
Status meaning only through color.status.{info,success,warning,danger,neutral}.{fg,bg,border,fill,on-fill}, always with an icon or words: never colour alone.
spectrum.* and set.* only for the purpose in their $extensions["org.design-library"].purpose (charts, identity), never for function.
Change colour in packages/core/tokens/colour.config.json, then npm run tokens; never edit tokens.colour.json.
Contrast: text 4.5:1 and non-text 3:1 in light, dark and both contrast levels; tokens:check refuses a theme that misses one.
decide: Is it text, a surface, a line or a control fill? Use the matching color.text*, color.bg*, color.border* or color.bg-control role.
Does it mean a status? Use color.status.* and add an icon or words.
Is it the brand action, link, focus or selection? It already reads the accent; don’t add another.
Is it a category in a chart or an identity? Use a declared set.* or spectrum.* with its purpose.
None fits: add a role through the colour config, never a literal.

frameworks.title: Spacing
rules: Hierarchy first: before choosing any space, write the page as a tree of groups (every element in exactly one group; members more related to one another than to anything outside). The page is the whole thing; its top-level groups come out of that analysis: header, page content (everything apart from the header and footer) and footer. Then give each group one gap by its depth, and frame only units that gain from being read alone.

Spacing and framing are one model: a frame is one unit in its parent group, placed at the parent's gap and measured from its outer edge; inside it, apply the method again (its content is a tree of its own, with its own gaps). The room between a frame's edge and its content is presentation, not a gap between groups, so it never breaks the inner-smaller-than-outer rule.
One 4 px base unit; components read roles (space.stack-pair, stack-item, stack-group, stack-section, inline-*, inset-*, gutter, margin-page), never a scale step.

Space inside a group is never larger than the space around it, at every node of the tree, the page's top level included: the page content sits from the header and the footer at least as far as its own units sit from one another (a frame is one unit, measured from its outer edge). SiteLayout builds that with its column's padding-block; a layout of your own gets it from the same tree, not from a page-specific rule.
One wrapper per group of the tree (a layout or a compound's part), owning only its children's gap: never one gap serving two levels.

Columns come from the same tree, after space and framing: give each group the columns its own content needs (a label column as wide as its longest label, the rest to the values; like members in equal tracks). A shared column runs only across the members whose alignment a reader sees (one list's terms), never from the page's grid, another panel or the window's breakpoint. If text wraps while space beside it in its row is unused, the column came from somewhere else: fix the group's columns, not the text.
The parent owns space: gap and padding on the container (Stack, Cluster, Grid gap props); never margins set by a sibling position.
Geometry never moves on hover, focus or loading: borders are always there, transparent at rest.
Targets are at least size.target (44 px), or size.target-dense in dense contexts.

Framing (Frame, a hero's `standalone`) isolates a piece and so interrupts reading: frame only what gains from being read alone (a brand opening, a statement, a quote, a call to action, a status message). Task and reference pages (tickets, schedules, lists, forms, settings, detail pages) never frame their heading away from their content: the title and intro sit with the task, which starts in the first view.
decide: Which level? Read it from the tree: the depth of the group whose children the space separates. Pairs (label and value): stack-pair. Items in a list: stack-item. Groups: stack-group. Sections: stack-section. The page content's units, and the page content from the header and footer: stack-page.
Side by side: inline-pair, inline-item, inline-group by the same levels.
Inside a surface: inset-* at the first content level, not on the wrapper.
Need a whole product denser or looser? Change the space option (compact, normal, loose, extra-loose), never single values.

About to frame something? Ask in order: what does the reader gain from seeing it alone? What did they come to this page to do? Would the frame push that below the first view? Nothing gained, or the task delayed: don't frame it. Gained: a stage for an opening (distraction-free when it's the page's only content, peek otherwise), a feature for a piece within the page.

frameworks.title: Visual noise
rules: Every mark (border, divider, fill, shadow, icon, colour, line of text) must carry information nothing else carries.
Cue order, cheapest first: space, alignment, type, tone, border, shadow. One cue per meaning.
Type is a cue: hierarchy comes from the type roles (type.*), not from extra colour, boxes or icons.
At most one enclosure per boundary; no box inside a box.
Transient affordances (drag handles, hover actions, customise cues) appear only while their state is active.
Approved components are never restyled as a side effect of another change.
decide: Can space or alignment group it? Stop there.
Else, can type weight or size? Then tone (a fill step). Then a full hairline. A shadow only if it floats.
Already inside an enclosure? Do not add another; separate with space.

frameworks.title: Elevation and layering
rules: Six levels: -1 sunken, 0 canvas, 1 raised, 2 chrome, 3 floating, 4 modal (packages/core/principles/elevation.json).
Tone first, shadow second, edge last. shadow.raised for anchored floating surfaces; shadow.overlay for free floating and modal. No shadow at rest on content or chrome.
z-index only as var(--layer-*) or a c.<part>.layer token aliasing one; never a number, never an inline zIndex.
Popups open in the top layer (popover attribute); dialogs as modal dialog elements; the layer token is only the fallback order.
A component ordering its own parts with layer.behind or layer.raised sets isolation: isolate on the holder.
decide: Pick the level from the ladder by what the surface does, then the layer by the "Choosing a layer" questions (elevation.json, printed below in the guide); the first yes decides.
Hidden behind something? Find the ancestor that starts a stacking context and move the thing to the top layer; never raise the number.

frameworks.title: Materials
rules: A component names its material (canvas, sunken, raised, tint, control, chrome, floating, modal, scrim, veil); tokens decide how it is painted.
The content layer (canvas, sunken, raised, tint, control) is always solid; only chrome and floating may be frosted.
Frosted is one global setting (data-material="frosted" or "solid" on the root); never per component.
Never glass on glass: a floating surface inside another is solid.
Reduced transparency, more contrast, forced colours and print are solid. Blur radius never animates.
Chrome, floating and modal surfaces carry data-material and data-elevation (the add-on seam).
decide: A page or region: canvas; rails and wells: sunken; a card or field: raised or control fill; the current item: tint.
A bar content scrolls under: chrome. A popup or free toolbar: floating. A blocking surface: modal over the scrim. Controls over media: veil.

frameworks.title: Motion
rules: Components read motion roles (duration.quick, change, move, move-far, shared; easing.standard, enter, exit, linear), never the private scale (fast, medium, slow).
Every visual value change (fill, border colour, shadow, opacity) eases at duration.change (200 ms); nothing jumps.
Content present in both states morphs (same wrapper, shared element) instead of disappearing and reappearing.
Zero latency where a person drives a value (typing, arrow-key steps, drags, sliders): no transition on that value (packages/core/motion/zero-latency.json).
With reduced motion travel snaps and fades stay; never transition: all; never a literal duration or curve.
decide: Does the person drive the value directly? No transition on it.
Is it a colour, fill, border, shadow or opacity change? duration.change with easing.standard.
Does something travel or resize? duration.move or move-far; arriving uses easing.enter, leaving easing.exit.
Is the same thing on both sides of a view change? A shared-element morph (duration.shared).

frameworks.title: States
rules: Every committed change is confirmed where it was made for at least duration.confirm-min.
Each state has one owner level (app, view, section, component, field) and one look: loading, saving, success, error, empty.
Views and sections load with shimmer skeletons; one bottom notification pill, one line, at most three.
Errors keep the input and always offer a recovery (Retry, Revert).
Empty states live in the content’s own wrapper and say why and what to do.
decide: Field-level change: the field shows pending, confirmed or failed (useCommit).
Whole view loading: a skeleton in the view, keeping the old view until the new one is ready.
A result of an action elsewhere: one notification pill that auto-dismisses.
Nothing to show: EmptyState inside the list or region, with the next action.

frameworks.title: Waiting
rules: Classify the wait: instant, responsive, waiting or long, and give the matching feedback.
Never block or lose input during a wait; keep the old view until the new one is ready.
One honest status; never a silent wait.
Indicators wait duration.indicator-delay before showing and stay at least duration.indicator-min.
decide: Under about 100 ms: no indicator. Up to about a second: a local indicator after the delay. Longer: progress with words. Very long: progress plus a way to keep working.

frameworks.title: Words
rules: Words come from content or props, never hard-coded in a component.
Sentence case, plain words, curly apostrophes; buttons are verbs that say the result.
Errors say what happened and how to fix it; never blame the person.
One name per thing across the product (the glossary).
Every icon-only control has an accessible name, shown by Tooltip.
decide: Label: the noun or the verb, two to four words.
Error: what happened, then the fix, in one or two short sentences.
Empty state: why it is empty, then the action.

frameworks.title: Showing information
rules: Run the reasoning chain in docs/visual-representation.md before choosing text, an icon, a picture, an illustration, media or a chart.
Show as is when accuracy, verbatim words or the content itself must be preserved.
Every visual carries a text alternative; charts never mislead (zero baselines for bars, honest scales).
Chart categories read set.* or spectrum.* with their declared purpose; status never by colour alone.
Inner bar segments stay square.
decide: Follow the agent procedure in docs/visual-representation.md (The chain as an agent procedure) and its Agent checklist.
